steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch pan.
Combine water and 1/3 cup flour in a heavy saucepan over medium heat; cook, whisking constantly, until thick. Transfer mixture to a large mixing bowl and set aside to cool, 15 to 20 minutes.
Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Mix in cocoa until smooth; remove from the heat and let cool, about 15 minutes.
Combine remaining 2 cups flour, baking powder, and salt in a small bowl, set aside. Add sugar and vanilla to cooled flour-water mixture; mix with an electric mixer until well combined.
Add cocoa mixture and mix until incorporated. Add dry flour mixture and stir until just blended; fold in walnuts.
Spread evenly in the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, 20 to 25 minutes. Cool before cutting into 20 squares.

raw_recipe.headline: Egg-Free Brownies
raw_recipe.description: Did you know you can make brownies without eggs? These chocolate brownies are a delicious treat and can be made vegan by using plant-based butter.

review.reviewBody: For those of us who are unable to use eggs in our baking, this is a winner! I have tried many times to make a brownie using different egg replacers and have never suceeded. Usually, it ends up a googey mess or just like a cake. This is great. I made 2 batches, the first exactly to recipe - came out a little cakey, but great taste. The second lot, I followed other reviewers suggestions and add enough milk to be able to "pour" the batter into the pan and also added about 1/2 cup of choc chips. This was fantastic!!!! (Not exactly like brownie made with eggs but very very close). Thank you for this recipe.

Perfect recipe! I actually dislike brownies with egg because they seem to take on that eggy taste, so this was a welcome find. Let's not forget that without eggs, it IS okay to lick the bowl afterward, another plus!

I Ihad to make a couple substitutions: 
1) only had a 9x9 baking pan, so I used it, just a thicker brownie that took about 10 minutes more to bake. I just kept checking every 5 minutes until the pick came out clean. Also oiled and floured the pan since I had no crisco and thought it would come out better ( my Kmart teflon coated pan isn't so nonstick anymore so this was a good move... and the brownies pulled away from the sides of the pan like they're supposed to.)

2) Used self-rising flour + 1 tsp baking powder instead of all purpose flour. This worked fine and the end result collapsed down a little in the middle but that wasn't an issue with the taste/texture - nice and fudgy, with a crunchy top crust, rather than cake-like. If you want cake brownies from this another half tsp of baking powder would likely do it.

3) Used the raw cane sugar you can get cheap at Aldi rather than white sugar... also worked fine and the unrefined raw cane has more "character."

Note: I think the trick for those who followed the recipe and got bad results is in the measuring. Baking is science and measurements need to be pretty precise for things to work like they should. Easy to make, delicious results! I decreased the flour to 1&1/2 cups, added chocolate chips instead of nuts, also added marshmallows and broken graham crackers. I used a 9x9 pan, which resulted in nice, thick brownies, but they did take longer to bake, about 32 minutes. Fantastic results!!

My kid has an egg and nut allergy, and I needed brownies for a school function. These were great! I read some of the reviews, and adjusted the recipe according to one reviewer's recommendation -- only because she had such strong conviction about her changes. I don't know what the original recipe tastes like, so maybe it's just as good, but here are the changes I made: instead of cocoa, I melted 4 squares of unsweetened (60%) chocolate bar with the butter; I reduced the dry flour mixture to 1 1/2 cups of flour; I reduced the baking powder to 1 teaspoon; and added a bunch of chocolate chips into the batter and on top. Yummy! Oh, maybe it's my oven, but I had to bake these a lot longer than 25 minutes.

I made this recipe gluten free as well due to a wheat allergy. Of course I made I wrong because I wrote it down 6 months ago and then tried to make it. I heated the water,butter and 1/3 c flour and put the cocoa in with the dry ingredients. I also cooked it in a 9 in round silicone pan in a toaster oven for 30 minutes and added ~.5 c of water for high altitude. The result was a very small cake like layer crust and the rest was chewy brownie so similar to the real kind you'd never know it was altered for allergies and altitude. 

I always use between 25-30% of leaveners due to altitude, 11000ft

OH MY!!! Was very nervous about making a brownie without eggs, but I really cannot stand the smell and taste of baked goods as much anymore since these two senses have become more sensitive as I have gotten older, and I stumbled upon this recipe and decided why not?! SOOOO glad I did, they are terrific, not sure what they are like made true to the recipe, I took the advice of a few reviewers and decreased the baking powder to 1 tsp and added an extra TBS of cocoa powder and some whole milk to the recipe to soften up the batter just before pouring to my pan. Added 1/2 C. of chocolate chips, too and voila! Soft and chocolately brownie goodness!!! Thank you for this great recipe.

This was so fun to make with my son. He was so happy that I found something without eggs that he has been waiting to eat in years.. The only thing I changed was to replace the nuts with chocolate chips due to nut allergies and the butter to margarine.. It came out soooo YUMMY.. all the family were surprised there was no eggs in it.. and it literally smelled like brownies in our home... I had to make another batch the next day ... :-)

Excellent, moist and fudgy! I incorporated the changes suggested (substituted 4 squares of baking chocolate, used less flour and baking powder, added 1 cup of chocolate chips, a splash of milk, etc.) and the family gobbled them up. I did not have the brownie pan size called for and used a slightly larger one, which made the brownies thinner than I would have liked, although they did require the full baking time. Next time, I'll either double the recipe or use a smaller pan. Thanks, everyone!

This is a very good recipe, I would not call it a brownie recipe but it is the best egg free moist chocolate cake I have ever had,I cut the flour to 1 1/2 cups and cut the sugar to 1cup, I also added almost a full block of chocolate in the butter before I added the cocoa powder and an extra half cup milk or water at the end of combining all ingredients, good almost mud cake like. I loved it

Easy to make. I cut the second amount of flour down to 1 1/2 cups as suggested in reviews. Added chocolate chips instead of walnuts.
I didn't have butter so I used same amount sour cream. Didn't have the right size baking tray so cooked for 15 minutes only.
Taste test: Amazing pit of 5 lol
Beautiful

WOW! I had no idea it was even possible to make egg-free brownies, let alone ones that were so good!! I halved the recipe, but kept the same chocolate amount as the original called for. I also threw in the walnuts, as well as a bit of chili powder. Needless to say, these brownies were all gone in less than 24 hours. (Much of that was my own doing, I must admit!) Thank you for sharing this great recipe. I will definitely use in the future.
So rich and dense and gooey… probably the best brownie I have EVER made! I used vegan butter and a 9 inch round pan. This recipe is 10/10. No notes!
Made it with Hersheys Special Dark chocolate and it tastes super good! Put caramel sauce on it too 😋

I made these for a family gathering aaaand instant hero. I didn't actually get high fives or a lot of extended compliments but you could kind of tell if you were looking. I used 1-1/2 cups of flour in the dry ingredients mix, and 1/2 cup of chocolate chips instead of nuts, and about 1/4 cup of milk in the complete mix. It cooked in about 30-35 minutes.
I love this recipe! The part about the flour was like intersting becase i didnt know which one was wihch. Mine turned out great anyways!
I had no eggs and wanted to make brownies for my family so I found this recipe and it was good for a no egg brownie recipe! Thanks for sharing!
Lovely recipe love it it is soft delicious and good for people who are lactose intolerance
This is disgusting. it took 1hr 30mins to cook and even then it was still bubbling. I've never seen a recipe that does this

This recipe was really great. Mine turned out more cakey than fudgey which is completely fine. They taste great and are very easy to make. I used hot chocolate mix because that’s all I had and it worked!!! Now I have peppermint hot chocolate brownies and the family loves them. Definitely making more as soon as these are gone.
I haven’t tried them yet (they are still in the oven) but I had one issue. The 9x13 pan was too big, so I had to use an 8x8
